page: Microsoft Azure D2s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server provides two vCPUs across a single physical x86_64 core utilizing hyperthreading. Hardware resources include 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside support for instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography. The server contains no local storage and no integrated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a pronounced split between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core tests reflect average performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1255.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1448.08, supported by stable single-threaded gzip compression at 24.0 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics fall into the lowest percentiles due to the limited two-thread allocation on a single execution core. Stress-ng multi-core (1906.49), Geekbench multi-core (1503.0), and PassMark CPU overall (2232.64) all rank in the bottom 10%, while uncached memory throughput measures 13.68 GB/sec for reads and 11.04 GB/sec for writes.

Cost efficiency is aligned with light-duty server roles where standard per-core memory capacity is required without paying for unneeded multi-core scaling or local disks. The reliance on remote storage introduces latency and throughput dependencies that must be planned for separately. Due to limited multi-threaded capacity and lower memory bandwidth, the D2s_v4 is poorly suited for compute-heavy parallel workloads, large-scale database operations, or memory-intensive caching. It serves best as a baseline host for light web serving, modest microservices, testing environments, and low-traffic enterprise utility applications.
